To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We present an index method for weighted-sequences, which is a two-dimensional structure consisting of a sequence of events with associated weights.

we propose an index structure for efficiently retrieving from a large weighted-sequence database all subsequences that match a given sequence both by events' occurrences and by weights, and that we demonstrate the applicability of the method in indexing scientific data for discovering correlations among numerical columns.
we propose and evaluate an index structure for weighted-sequences that enables efficient retrieval of subsequences that match a given pattern both in terms of events and weights.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of a new index structure for efficiently managing weighted-sequences and retrieving from the database subsequences matching a given pattern.
indexing large sequence databases and finding patterns in the data.
the development of efficient indexing methods for managing large databases of weighted sequences, which are ubiquitous in scientific and business domains.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method proposed in this paper provides an efficient way for indexing weighted-sequences in a sequence database.
the proposed index structure is effective and efficient for indexing and querying large sequence databases.
the index structure proposed enables one to efficiently retrieve from a large sequence database all subsequences that match a given sequence pattern both by events and weights.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed index structure is able to retrieve subsequences with a given pattern of events and their weights from large databases in a very short amount of time.
the proposed index structure can support a broad range of pattern queries on weighted-sequences, and is particularly useful for the discovery of correlations in scientific data.

our index structure enables us to efficiently search for all subsequences in a large sequence database whose events follow a given pattern and whose weights follow a given pattern, and whose weights are not uniform.
The main takeaway from our work is that
indexing a sequence by its weights is as important as indexing the sequence by its events.
the indexing of weighted-sequences is an effective approach for the discovery of patterns in large databases.
the proposed indexing method can be applied to any sequence database that has a nonuniform event frequency distribution.
